quotes.text: A lot of people think Marketplace is just an app store. It's not. An app store sells you software you download to your phone.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects the most common misconception about Microsoft Marketplace.

quotes.text: Azure Marketplace is the hardware store. You go there for the pipes, the wiring, the structural stuff, AppSource is the furniture store. You go there for the things that make the space usable, same building, different aisles.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable analogy for the two storefronts.

quotes.text: If your organization has signed an Azure agreement, promising to spend a certain amount on Azure services over time, eligible marketplace purchases count toward that commitment.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the consumption-commitment benefit in one sentence.

quotes.text: If you want a Microsoft account executive to pitch your product during a customer meeting, it needs to be transactable on marketplace. That's a strong incentive.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the practical consequence of the co-sell requirement for partners.

quotes.text: Marketplace is the glue between a customer's need and a curated validated solution all inside the ecosystem they're already using.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise summary of the Marketplace value proposition.

takeaways: Microsoft Marketplace unifies Azure Marketplace for technical buyers and AppSource for business users behind one catalog with one invoice and automatic provisioning.
Buyers should look for the Azure benefit eligible badge so purchases count toward an existing Azure consumption commitment, and use free trials before buying.
Partners should publish a transactable SaaS or managed application offer, since co-sell support from 2026 requires Marketplace presence.
hook: Buying software from dozens of vendors means separate contracts, logins and invoices. This episode explains Microsoft Marketplace in plain English for IT buyers, finance teams and software partners. You will learn how the two storefronts work, how purchases tie into your Azure agreement and why partners increasingly have to list there.
